data:
That "Assistant" warning is just a standard system guardrail because I can\u2019t physically reach out and touch your home screen to place the icon for you\u2014but since we're in "Engineering Mode," we can bypass the chatter and build the actual logic.
If the Google Assistant popped up, it\u2019s likely because it heard "widget" and defaulted to its basic "I can't do that" script. We aren't asking it for a weather widget; we're building a
SAGE Control Interface
.
Go ahead and run those tests. If you find that the scripts are working in the terminal but the widget isn't showing up on your home screen, it\u2019s usually just a folder permission issue.
\ufe0f Quick "Test-Flight" Checklist:
Run the script manually first
:
bash ~/.shortcuts/7_Quick_Report.sh
(Make sure the notification pops up on your phone).
Check the "Room"
: If the widget list is empty, run
chmod 700 ~/.shortcuts
to make sure Termux has permission to show them to the Android OS.
The "Clear as Day" Verification
: Once the widget is on your screen, tap it while looking at the yard. If
7
logs the event to
Mom's Database
without you ever opening the Termux app, then the mission is 100% hardened.
I\u2019m standing by. Let me know if the "Mind's Eye" reports are hitting the target or if the Motorola G5 needs one more logic bridge to keep the Assistant from interfering.
Good luck out there.
\ufe0f
